problem: Prior route-instruction generators rely on hand-crafted rules/templates (rigid, unnatural, poor generalization) or, like Oswald et al., learn content selection but retrieve existing human sentences instead of composing new ones.
motivation: Robots that guide humans in unknown indoor environments (no GPS) must decide what to say and phrase it naturally, since instruction quality determines whether people can follow it. Content selection preferences vary by population and environment, so they should be learned from human demonstrations, not hand-coded.
key_idea: Split instruction generation into content selection (MaxEnt IRL policy over CAS structures plus ambiguity-checked attribute filling) and surface realization (an LSTM encoder-aligner-decoder that translates formal CAS commands into English, reranked by an LSTM language model).
insight: Learned content selection plus neural translation yields instructions people follow at least as accurately as human ones, partly because the pipeline explicitly checks ambiguity (Eq. P(c|p,m)) and uses only visible landmarks. The aligner ablation shows only a small sentence-BLEU gain (74.67 vs 74.40) but a larger corpus-BLEU gain (60.10 vs 57.40), and the LM reranking removes ungrammatical candidates. The human study shows that BLEU understates quality, since generated instructions were followed more often than the human references.
method: Compound Action Specification (CAS): formal logic language (Travel, Turn, Face, Verify, Find) with attributes, used as an intermediate representation between paths and language; human instructions are converted to CAS via MARCO.

Content selection via MaxEnt IRL: MDP whose state is 14 binary context features and whose actions are CAS structures described by 9 property features; the MAP property vector is matched to k_c=100 nearest CAS structures using mutual-information-weighted distance, then spectral clustering yields candidate structures.
Sentence planning: fill attribute values greedily using only follower-visible objects; keep commands whose validity/unambiguity likelihood P(c|p,m) exceeds threshold P_t=0.99.

Surface realization: 2-layer LSTM encoder (input reversed) with Bahdanau-style attention aligner and 2-layer LSTM decoder with deep output, 128 units, trained with NLL on CAS-to-instruction pairs; greedy and beam search candidates.
Language model reranking: 2-layer LSTM LM assigns perplexity to candidate sentences and the lowest-perplexity one is chosen per path segment; segment sentences are concatenated.
Data augmentation: rule-based substitution of attribute values in command-instruction pairs, expanding to about 750k train and 190k validation pairs.

setting.backbone: MaxEnt IRL policy + LSTM encoder-aligner-decoder + LSTM language model (trained from scratch)
setting.training_data: SAIL route instruction corpus (3213 demonstrations, 706 paragraphs, 126 paths, 3 virtual environments), 70/10/20 split, rule-augmented to about 750k training pairs; LM trained on English data
setting.observation: symbolic hybrid metric-topologic-semantic map and path (no images)
setting.action_space: not applicable (text generation); IRL actions are CAS structures
setting.simulator: SAIL virtual environments (MARCO); custom 3D first-person virtual world for human evaluation
setting.privileged: ground-truth map with object/feature annotations and the shortest path given as input

numbers.extra: trained with rule-based data augmentation; BLEU against human references
numbers.evidence: On the test set, the method achieves sentence- and corpus level BLEU scores of 72.18% and 45.39%

numbers.backbone: IRL + LSTM encoder-decoder (last hidden state) + LSTM LM
numbers.evidence: Table: Aligner ablation results, No Aligner 74.40 / 57.40

numbers_note: Human-evaluation results (accuracy vs. distance from goal) are given only in figures; the text gives relative differences: +4% exact goal reach, +8% within one vertex, 6% lower failure (d>2), 9.52 s less time, 72% vs 52% rated easy. No standard navigation benchmark is used.
results: Generated instructions reach sentence-level BLEU 72.18 and corpus-level 45.39 on the SAIL test set, and 74.67 / 60.10 on validation. In a 441-trial MTurk study with 42 participants, people followed the generated instructions as accurately as or better than the human ones (4% more exact arrivals, 6% lower failure) and rated them easier (72% vs 52%).
limitations: Only generates instructions for the shortest path in small simulated indoor environments from a single dataset (SAIL) with a symbolic map; no real robot or perception.
Automatic BLEU is a weak proxy, and the human study is small (441 trials, 50 paths) with the time difference not statistically significant; no comparison against other generation baselines.
Pipeline relies on hand-designed CAS representation, feature sets, and retrieval, and is slow (33 s per path on a CPU).
builds_on: Mei et al. 2016 (listen, attend, walk; selective generation)
compares_to: Human-written SAIL instructions (reference and human baseline)
